To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have generated an HLA‐A2 restricted, breast cancer‐associated CTL that recognizes HLA‐A‐2 bound, peptide antigens.
a breast cancer‐reactive CTL was generated by stimulating normal PRL against an HLA class I matched breast cancer line.
we have generated tumor‐specific CTL from a healthy donor against HLA‐class‐I matched HBL‐100 breast cancer cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of breast cancer‐specific peptides presented by HLA‐class molecules.
the identification of tumor‐specific antigens recognized by the immune system.
the development of immunotherapy for cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HBL‐ 100 CTL line is HLA‐A*0201 restricted and recognizes an epitope(s) associated with HLA class I molecules of breast cancer cell lines, but not of non‐breast cancer cell lines.
the tumor‐reactive CTL line BL.HBL‐ 100 was generated from a normal healthy human donor PBL by stimulating the PBL against the HLA‐A*0101 matched breast cancer cell‐line HBL‐100 (Fig. 1).

a CTL was produced that recognized a peptide(s) bound to HLA‐1 that was derived from a breast cancer cell line and not recognized by CTL produced from normal PBL stimulated by an unrelated HLA‐class 1 matched cell line.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we generated a CTL line from a healthy donor by stimulating his PBL with irradiated, partially HLA‐class‐I matched breast cancer cell lines (HBL‐100).
we have shown that a tumor reactive CTL line was generated by stimulating PBL from a healthy donor with HLA‐A*0101 partially matched breast cancer cells.

we have shown that a breast cancer‐reactive, MHC‐restricted CTL line can be generated by stimulating normal peripheral blood lymphocytes with an irradiated HLA‐matched breast cancer cell line, that this CTL line recognizes HLA‐A2+ breast cancer cells but not HLA A2+ non‐breast cancer cell lines, that the CTL line recognizes peptides presented in the HLA‐A class I molecule, and that the peptides that are recognized by the CTL reside in fraction
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can isolate tumor‐reactive CTLs that can be used to identify tumor‐specific antigens.
it is possible to generate CTL from a normal healthy individual that can recognize and lyse HLA‐A*0201+, breast cancer cells.
we have identified an immunogenic peptide derived from the breast cancer cell line, HBL‐100, that is recognized by an HLA‐A*0201 restricted CTL line generated against the HBL‐200 cell line.
